record.paper_title: $p$-matchings in graphs: a brief survey with some open problems
record.original_question: For a finite graph G, define a disconnected matching to be a matching M such that either |M|=1 or the induced subgraph G[M] on the endpoints of edges in M is disconnected. Let β_dc(G)=max{|M|: M is a disconnected matching in G}. What is the computational complexity of determining β_dc(G), equivalently of deciding, given G and an integer k, whether G has a disconnected matching of size at least k?

evidence.quote: Example 3.5 (Disconnected matching). A matching M is disconnected if |M| = 1 or <M> is disconnected. We have beta_dc(G) = max{|M| : M is disconnected matching} and beta_dc^-(G) = min{|M| : M is maximal disconnected matching}.
Of the matching varieties discussed in Section 3, this leaves only the complexity of beta_dc in question.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G=(V,E) be a finite simple graph. A matching M⊆E is a set of pairwise vertex-disjoint edges. Write V(M) for the set of endpoints of the edges of M, and G[V(M)] for the subgraph of G induced by V(M). Call M a disconnected matching if either |M|=1 or the induced subgraph G[V(M)] is disconnected. Define
   β_dc(G) = max{ |M| : M is a disconnected matching of G }.

Determine the computational complexity of computing β_dc(G); equivalently, classify the complexity of the decision problem: given a finite graph G and an integer k, decide whether G admits a disconnected matching of size at least k.
artifact.status_search_result: The decision problem for disconnected matchings was shown to be NP-complete by Gomes, Masquio, Pinto, dos Santos and Szwarcfiter ("Disconnected Matchings", arXiv:2112.09248, published in Theoretical Computer Science, 2023). They prove NP-completeness even on bounded-diameter bipartite graphs, and provide further complexity results (NP-completeness on chordal graphs when the number of components is part of the input, polynomial-time algorithms on interval graphs, FPT under treewidth, etc.). Thus the complexity question about β_dc has been resolved (it is NP-hard in general, with a fine-grained complexity landscape across graph classes).

status_evidence.title: Disconnected Matchings (arXiv:2112.09248)
status_evidence.snippet: For every fixed c ≥ 2, the problem of finding c-disconnected matchings is NP-complete even on bounded-diameter bipartite graphs; polynomial for c=1.
status_evidence.claim: Deciding existence of a disconnected matching of size ≥ k is NP-complete, resolving the complexity of β_dc.

status_evidence.title: Disconnected matchings - ScienceDirect (Theoretical Computer Science, 2023)
status_evidence.snippet: Published version of the disconnected matchings paper establishing NP-completeness and further complexity dichotomies.
status_evidence.claim: The complexity of computing β_dc has been settled: NP-hard in general with refined results on structured graph classes.
